chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Abū Isḥāq, from Nūḥ ibn Shuʿayb al-Khurāsānī, from Yāsīn, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A well into which a drop of blood or wine has fallen. He said: “Blood, wine, carrion, and pig meat are all the same in that regard: twenty buckets are to be drawn from it; and if the odor prevails, it should be drawn from until it becomes wholesome.”

And the report narrated by al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād, from Kurdawayh, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a well into which a drop of blood, intoxicating nabīdh, urine, or wine falls. He said: “Thirty buckets are to be drawn from it.”

So these two are one report, and because of them it is not possible to reject all of these reports. If we act upon the earlier reports, we will also be acting upon these two reports, because when all the water, or a kurr of it, is drawn out, then the thirty buckets are included within that. But if we were to act upon these two reports, we would be rejecting those others in their entirety and not adopting anything of their rulings.

As for what he considered regarding the alternating of four men in drawing the water when drawing all of it is difficult, this is indicated by the report which we narrated earlier from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Hilāl, who said: I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about what falls into the well, and he mentioned various things, until he said: when I reached the donkey and the camel, he said: “A kurr of water.”

And if it is abundant, four men alternate in drawing the water for one day, which exceeds a kurr of water and does not fall short, and it must be sufficient. And because the alternating of men is taken into consideration regarding what falls into the water and changes its color or taste, while drawing all of it is difficult. Do you not see that...

key_terms.بِئْرٌ: a well used as the subject of rulings on water contamination
key_terms.تَرَاوُحِ أَرْبَعَةِ رِجَالٍ: the alternating of four men in drawing water when complete removal is difficult
key_terms.ثَلَاثُونَ دَلْوًا: thirty buckets to be drawn as stated in another report
key_terms.خَمْرٍ: wine, treated here as an impure contaminant
key_terms.عِشْرُونَ دَلْوًا: twenty buckets to be drawn as stated in one report
key_terms.قَطْرَةُ دَمٍ: a drop of blood falling into the well
key_terms.كُرٌّ مِنْ مَاءٍ: a kurr of water, a legal measure used in purification rulings
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: water is drawn out from the well for purification

ai.seo_question: How many buckets must be drawn from a well if blood, wine, urine, or other impurities fall into it?
ai.summary: This passage addresses the purification of well water when small amounts of impure substances fall into it, specifying amounts of water to be drawn out. It also discusses reconciling apparently differing hadith reports and mentions the practice of rotating four men to draw water when removing all of it is difficult. The focus is on legal rulings of ritual purity and the handling of najasah in water.
